title: The Séance at Madame Weil's
teaser: Madame Weil promised that tonight the spirits would speak a name. The candles went out for one minute, the circle of hands broke, and when the light returned the medium was no longer breathing, and the planchette on the spirit board stood on the word "Farewell". Around the table sat people who had paid her for séances for years, and each of them had something to fear if the spirits told the truth.

habits.label: Phosphor on the fingers
clues: In the machinery closet, three greenish fingerprints glow in the dark on the handle of the machine that taps out the spirits' answers. The culprit has phosphorescent paint on their fingers.
In Madame's study a smudged fingerprint glows on an envelope from her black folder. The culprit has phosphor on their fingertips.

habits.label: Smells of incense
clues: In the coach yard, out in the frost and far from any censer, there's a sweet smell of incense by the car door. The culprit smells of incense.
The curtain between the waiting room and the corridor smells of incense, though it's never burned in the waiting room. The culprit smells of church incense.

habits.label: Gauze threads
habits.habit: Gauze threads clinging to their sleeves
clues: A white gauze thread, the stuff Madame made her "ectoplasm" from, hangs on a nail by the attic stairs. The culprit has gauze threads on their sleeves.
There are a few gauze fibres on a velvet armchair in the tea parlour, and gauze is kept only in the closet. The culprit has gauze threads on their clothes.

habits.label: Singed cuff
habits.habit: A cuff singed by a candle
clues: A charred scrap of cambric torn from a cuff lies by the candlestick in the séance room. The culprit has a singed cuff.
The cook saw someone in the waiting room hurriedly beating out a little flame on their sleeve. The culprit's cuff was singed by a candle.

habits.label: Mourning armband
habits.habit: A black mourning armband on their sleeve
clues: The caretaker saw a black band flash on someone's sleeve in the half-dark of the attic stairs. The culprit wears a mourning armband.
A scrap of black crepe with a pinhole hangs on a little nail by the door of the machinery closet. The culprit wears a mourning armband on their sleeve.

habits.label: Evil eye charm
habits.habit: A blue glass eye against the evil eye on a cord
clues: A chipped piece of blue glass with a white pupil was found under the workbench in the machinery closet. The culprit has an evil eye charm.
The cook in the tea parlour saw someone whisper over a little blue glass eye and tuck it under their collar. The culprit wears an evil eye charm.

habits.label: Amber cigarette holder
habits.habit: Smokes through a long amber cigarette holder
clues: By the coach yard gates there's a cigarette end with a neatly flattened tip and no lip marks, the kind a holder leaves. The culprit smokes through a holder.
There's a crumb of honey-coloured amber on the carpet in Madame's study, chipped off something thin and hollow. The culprit has an amber cigarette holder.

habits.label: Bowler hat
habits.habit: Never takes off their bowler hat, even indoors
clues: A black silk hatband, the kind bowlers have, lies on the top step of the attic stairs. The culprit wears a bowler hat.
The cook grumbled that a black bowler bobbed at the table in the tea parlour all evening, like in a tavern. The culprit never takes off their bowler, even indoors.

habits.label: Smells of petrol
clues: Madame's glove, which was held in the circle of hands in the séance room, smells of petrol. The culprit smells of petrol.
There's an oily stain on the waiting room carpet by the coat stand with a sharp smell of petrol. The culprit smells of petrol.

habits.label: Cracks their knuckles
clues: The cook heard a dry cracking behind the door of Madame's study, like breaking biscuits, and only later realised it was knuckles. The culprit cracks their knuckles.
The caretaker by the attic stairs heard rapid clicking of joints from above, like someone impatient. The culprit cracks their knuckles when nervous.

habits.label: Liquorice pastilles
clues: There's a black liquorice pastille wrapper on a saucer in the tea parlour, and Madame couldn't stand liquorice. The culprit chews liquorice pastilles.
On the spirit board in the séance room, right by the word "Farewell", there's a sticky black spot with the aniseed smell of liquorice. The culprit chews liquorice.

habits.label: Pince-nez on a chain
habits.habit: Wears pince-nez on a thin chain
clues: An oval lens from a pince-nez lies on the box of bells in the machinery closet. The culprit wears pince-nez.
The caretaker saw lenses flash and a chain swing in the lamplight in the coach yard. The culprit wears pince-nez on a chain.

habits.label: Bitten nails
clues: On the velvet tablecloth in the séance room, by one of the chairs, there are little crescents of bitten nails. The culprit bites their nails.
Under an armchair in the tea parlour there's a little heap of bitten nails: the wait was long and nervous. The culprit bites their nails.

habits.label: Kid gloves
habits.habit: Never takes off thin kid gloves
clues: A drawer of the desk in Madame's study was pulled out, but there isn't a single print on the lacquer, only the matt trace of thin leather. The culprit never takes off their kid gloves.
A scrap of pale kid with a mother-of-pearl button is caught on the coach yard gates. The culprit wears thin kid gloves.

habits.label: Coin in the fingers
habits.habit: Rolls a silver coin through their fingers
clues: The errand boy in the waiting room remembered a silver coin rolling nonstop over someone's knuckles. The culprit rolls a coin through their fingers.
Under the wheel of the tapping machine in the machinery closet there was an old silver coin rubbed mirror-bright by fingers. The culprit has a habit of rolling a coin through their fingers.

habits.label: Scar on the palm
habits.habit: A white scar right across their palm
clues: The dusty rail of the attic stairs has a palm print crossed by a neat pale line. The culprit has a scar on their palm.
In Madame's study her notebook has a note: "White scar across the palm. Ask the spirits where from." The culprit has a scar right across their palm.

safe: The fireproof safe in Madame's study was opened with the combination, and the black folder of clients' letters has vanished. The culprit knows the safe combination.
Behind a still life in the tea parlour there's a small safe even the cook didn't know about: the door is locked as before, but it's empty inside. The culprit knows the safe combination.
keys: Madame always locked the machinery closet herself, yet tonight it was opened with a key, and the lock hasn't a scratch. The culprit had keys.
The coach yard gates are padlocked at night, yet by midnight the padlock hung open on its hasp. The culprit had keys.
medic: The cup Madame drank from before the séance in the tea parlour has a bitter sediment, the dose timed for exactly an hour. The culprit knows about poisons.
Madame's handkerchief in the séance room has a colourless stain smelling of bitter almonds. The culprit knows about poisons.
tech: The candles in the séance room are blown out by a blower under the table, and its motor was switched on bypassing Madame's switch. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
In the machinery closet the wire from the machine that knocks for the spirits was moved to another terminal, and the knocking came from an empty room. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
cash: A whole week's takings are gone from the deposit box in the waiting room, yet the ledger balances. The culprit had access to money.
A bank receipt lies in Madame's study: yesterday a large sum was withdrawn from her account, and the signature is a flawless forgery. The culprit had access to money.
passages: A little door behind a black curtain, unknown to the clients, leads from the machinery closet to the séance room, and its bolt is drawn back. The culprit knows the service passages.
The attic stairs can only be reached through the pantry behind the kitchen, and fresh footprints in the dust lead from exactly there. The culprit knows the service passages.
driver: The car in the coach yard isn't where it was left in the evening, and its radiator is still warm. The culprit can drive.
In Madame's study the car key lies on the desk, though it's kept in a drawer, and six more kilometres show on the car's meter. The culprit can drive.
sched: By the script, the candles in the séance room go out at exactly midnight for exactly one minute, and the guests aren't warned. The culprit knows the schedule.
Someone went into Madame's study during the quarter hour when the cook clears the crockery from the tea parlour and the corridor is empty. The culprit knows the schedule.
quiet: The attic stairs creak even under a cat, yet the cook behind the wall didn't hear a sound. The culprit moves silently.
In the minute of darkness in the séance room someone walked round the table, and nobody in the circle heard footsteps. The culprit moves silently.
strong: In the machinery closet the cast-iron counterweight from the spirit-knocking machine was lifted off its hook and set on the floor, and it weighs as much as a sack of coal. The culprit is physically strong.
The prop trunk on the attic stairs landing, which took three people to haul up, has been pushed against the wall. The culprit is physically strong.
tools: The lock on the bureau in Madame's study was taken apart and put back together, the spring in place, not a scratch on the brass. The culprit is handy with tools.
The mouthpiece of the speaking tube by the attic stairs was unscrewed and screwed back on, with fresh spanner marks on the nuts. The culprit is handy with tools.
french: "Elle sait tout", French for "She knows everything", is pencilled on the back of a tarot card in the séance room. The culprit knows French.
The last entry in the visitors' book in the waiting room is in French without a single mistake: "Les morts ne mentent pas", "The dead don't lie". The culprit knows French.
